entry.title: How Wildfire Investigators Determine a Fire's Cause | South Dakota Firefighters Tell Their Stories

media:group.media:title: How Wildfire Investigators Determine a Fire's Cause | South Dakota Firefighters Tell Their Stories
media:group.media:description:
A Weather Channel Mini-Documentary
Long after the flames are out, a wildfire leaves behind a trail of evidence. Elite fire investigators are trained to read it. Fire investigators walk the burn, narrowing the blaze indicators down through what they call the "area of confusion" until they reach the ignition area. Char acts as a compass and grass points back toward where the fire came from. Once they've pinned the origin, the question shifts to how it started, a jigsaw puzzle of witnesses, weather, fuels and physical evidence that feeds directly into preventing the next fire.
This film is part of a special Weather Channel mini-documentary series exploring the people, places and experiences behind extreme weather and natural disasters. Through immersive storytelling and firsthand accounts, the series goes beyond the forecast to reveal what it’s really like to live through, and fight, the forces of nature.

entry.title: How "Super El Niño" Could Cause Worldwide Weather Chaos

media:group.media:title: How "Super El Niño" Could Cause Worldwide Weather Chaos
media:group.media:description:
El Niño isn’t just back—it’s charging in with a vengeance.
The Climate Prediction Center warns this event could hyper-drive into a "Super El Niño"—a globally disruptive atmospheric monster. When the Pacific Ocean overheats like this, it turns the planet's entire weather engine upside down.
Meteorologist Mike Bettes shows us what happens when global weather patterns run wild.

entry.title: What It’s Really Like Inside a Wildfire | South Dakota Firefighters Tell Their Stories

media:group.media:title: What It’s Really Like Inside a Wildfire | South Dakota Firefighters Tell Their Stories
media:group.media:description:
A Weather Channel Mini-Documentary
What does a wildfire actually sound like when you’re standing inside it? What does it smell like? How does the heat feel, and what stays with you after the flames are gone?
In this Weather Channel mini-documentary, wildland firefighters and pilots in South Dakota take you inside the experience of fighting a wildfire, describing the sounds, smells, heat and sights they encounter up close, from the deep rumble of flames to the whistle of falling slurry.
Fire management officers, fire prevention specialists and single-engine air tanker pilots with South Dakota Wildland Fire also share the moments they can’t unsee—and the stress that can continue long after a wildfire is out.
